author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Two synthetic scenario packs written for this benchmark in the README vocabulary (a 6-step workshop-fire pack with alarm/call/evacuate/extinguish/unsafe re-entry/fire door, delayed and conditional events, three timed cues and two outcomes; and a one-event chance pack), played by an independent stdlib rule engine (ref.py) whose semantics are listed in engine_semantics; scripted playthroughs covering outcomes, UNRESOLVED/IN_PROGRESS boundaries, cue windows, unsafe decisions and alternatives, replay truncation, budget and order; 12 randomized playthroughs (seed 20260916); 10 seeded chance runs using mulberry32/FNV-1a from their public definitions; 14 import validation cases (refusals, dead end, unreachable item); and property checks on the five built-in packs. The built-in content is illustrative and is not re-derived.
reference_citations: tools.petrov.re spec 16 Emergency Drill Simulator (MVP scope, model rules, QA, acceptance criteria) and spec 00-common (syntax/data and state checks)
tools.petrov.re README-emergencydrill.txt manifest revision 2026-09-15.emergencydrill.r3, sections 3-4 (vocabulary and rule IDs only)
Fowler/Noll/Vo, FNV hash, FNV-1a 32-bit (offset basis 2166136261, prime 16777619), http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/index.html
Rule-engine and graph first principles: bench/emergencydrill/ref.py (stdlib)
tolerance: All checks exact (categorical outcomes, id lists, integer state, booleans): the model is a discrete rule engine where any difference is a logic difference, not numerical error. The only real-valued check (first mulberry32 draw) uses abs 1e-12, far below the 2^-32 output resolution.
engine_semantics: Step t = 1..step_limit. Observations (cues) for step t are evaluated on the state after step t-1; a cue 'appears' at the first such step whose condition holds.
At step t: selection size must be <= actions_per_step (else refused); every selected decision must be available on the state before step t (else, on replay, the run stops before step t, DRILL-M-007).

Selected decisions apply in declared order, then events in declared order, each event at most once per run, each seeing the state left by what ran before it in that step; condition 'step' = t; since(mark) = t - step at which mark was set, false if unset.
A chance event whose condition holds draws one number u from mulberry32((seed XOR FNV-1a-32(scenario id)) >>> 0) and fires iff u < chance; no other draws.
After the step, outcome = first declared outcome whose condition holds (DRILL-D-005); none at step_limit -> UNRESOLVED (DRILL-M-006); run ended early without outcome -> IN_PROGRESS.

A cue is missed when no expected decision was taken at any step <= appear+window-1 and the run has completed that step (DRILL-D-001); unsafe decisions list the declared safer alternatives available at that step (DRILL-D-002).
Variables are clamped to README ranges (hazard 0-4, comms/ext 0-2, counts >= 0); the synthetic packs never reach a bound through an effect.

not_benchmarked: Content correctness of the five built-in scenarios (illustrative, no source-level emergency procedure pack); spec requires review by a competent emergency professional - not done.
Real-world fire/gas/injury dynamics: out of scope by spec.

Chance-draw consumption model (one draw per chance event whose condition holds) and window-end boundary are this author's reading of the README; if the tool differs, chance-* and window cases fail on semantics, not safety.
Selecting a decision that becomes available only after another decision in the same step (availability re-check within a step) - ambiguous, not asserted.
Whether a cue whose window has not ended when the run ends counts as missed - not asserted (pending cues omitted).
Branch comparison UI, PDF debrief layout, rewind, localisation, image assets, 390 px layout - UI/QA properties.
Built-in state-space sizes quoted in the README (15 611 ... 97 662) - pack content unseen, not re-derived.
Language-completeness rules for imports (warnings) - tool contract without independent basis.
Human-factors training effectiveness - spec forbids psychometric claims.
coverage: Spec 16 headline claims: rule-based state evolution with decisions then events; deterministic seeded replay; permalink scenario+seed+decisions; limited decisions per step; multiple paths to an outcome (fast/slow controlled); debrief outputs scenario_outcome, key decisions (timeline), missed_cues, barriers_used with trace, unsafe decisions with safer alternatives; no reward for dangerous action; step limit / unfinished runs never safe-looking; schema validation before load with refusals; reachability and dead-end detection; built-in packs' acceptance properties (no timer, no speed score, IDs on debrief items, no real-world prediction claim).
